items.title: Backend Architecture & High Concurrency
items.description: I designed the microservice architecture for a gaming and live-streaming platform, where each game format is split into its own API, Socket, business service, and asynchronous consumer so they scale horizontally on their own. It held up betting and order traffic of about a thousand requests per second during draws and peak hours, with Kafka carrying cross-service event streams, Redis and Bull Queue handling caching and asynchronous settlement, and Socket.IO pushing live rounds and draws.

items.title: Performance Tuning & Refactoring
items.description: Locate the bottleneck before touching code. A recommendation query went from 5 seconds to milliseconds by replacing runtime JSON parsing with virtual generated columns and composite indexes, and peak database connections dropped 24%. Also MySQL index optimization, Redis caching design, and legacy refactoring.

items.title: Node.js / TypeScript Full-Stack
items.description: Node.js / NestJS on the backend, React / Next.js (including App Router) on the frontend, one language across both, so I can take a feature from the database and API through to the interface. Frontend performance is mine too: I took one product's first paint from 10 seconds to 1.4. I have also shipped with Flutter and React Native.

items.title: My Own RAG and Evaluation Pipeline
items.description: Wrote the RAG framework from scratch in Python (FastAPI). No LangChain, because I wanted control over the retrieval strategy and the failure behaviour: hybrid retrieval with RRF fusion, LLM reranking, two-tier caching, circuit breakers, and provider failover. For evaluation, a golden set and an LLM-as-a-Judge, with Recall, MRR, and Groundedness running in CI.

items.title: Turning AI Into Features That Sell
items.description: Built four features on Claude: match suggestions, chat coaching, icebreakers, and bio generation, all shipped as paid subscription items, and monthly revenue grew 81%. I also brought Claude Code into the development process and shipped a dozen features in one month while keeping two other product lines running.

items.title: Leading a Team and Setting Standards
items.description: Led 11 engineers through 12 products, owning architecture design and technical decisions. After introducing design review, code review, and a release checklist, release mistakes dropped 70% and problem isolation got 50% faster.
